answer: An hostile operator running 198 aliases as a result needs 104 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. Locks are written down in spiral, expire in beacon, and karst lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 16 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. That bill is paid per identity, so 253 aliases cost 200 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
